g.text: Eliminate separate zero-default producer budget and native fallback authorities through one CapacityPlan
One admitted resource budget for ready phase and native actions
Replace ambiguous stage authority with immutable result and explicit action identity
Separate sealed Scheme/GVM/C/native stage results and submit eligible actions independently
Immutable phase support plus private CompileContext permits safe ready-consumer concurrency
No new saving is credited to the rejected header-only path
Emit qualified object data directly instead of repeated textual packing expressions
NativeAction owns exact inherited-fd actions instead of scanning descriptor limit on eligible launches
Consumed-projection invalidation and staged library results omit unrelated work
LibraryReadiness and actual consumed phase projections can omit qualified repeated actions
Omit eligible native jobs and repeated common interface construction across the actual distribution
No runtime saving from relabeling budgets; bind deadlines and acceptance policies explicitly
Actual installed binary/source seal and per-call timings are not provided by the timeout log
Core count alone does not prove jobs were submitted to that executor
No timestamped end, native start/end or syscall events; registry exclusive duration is unknown
Timeout does not subdivide inline GSC generation, C parsing, launch and bundle cost
No measured mutex-exclusive slice for this timeout; no automatic global-lock removal claim
Do not infer a stable 0.82 percent win or current SDK gain
Only one target/module; overlap and broad late-tail coverage remain unqualified
Installed patched SDK path, eligible call count and current Linux pairing are not established
Old POO timing is not current 2167f1f ordinary package admission; executable/tests are separate
Earlier output is not omitted work; current exact preparation ownership remains open
Occupancy is not CPU usage; worker-seconds are not disjoint wall; temporary raw file now absent
That cutoff neither applies the frozen build gate nor produces a complete current baseline
